ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the bracket is fixed on the horizontal ground, and its inclined smooth straight rod makes an angle of $30^{\circ}$ with the ground. Two rings A and B are threaded on the straight rod and are connected by a light rope passing over a smooth fixed pulley. The size of the pulley is negligible, and the whole device is in the same vertical plane. When the rings are in equilibrium, rope OA is vertical, and the angle between rope OB and the straight rod is $30^{\circ}$. Then the mass ratio of rings A and B is (　　)

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, the bracket is fixed on the horizontal ground, and its inclined smooth straight rod makes an angle of $30^{\circ}$ with the ground. Two rings A and B are threaded on the straight rod and are connected by a light rope passing over a smooth fixed pulley. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a smooth straight rod placed obliquely on the horizontal ground, and the straight rod and the horizontal ground are marked as forming a 30° angle; two rings A and B are both sleeved on this inclined rod, with A at a higher position and B at a lower position. Above there is a smooth fixed pulley O, and a light rope passes over the pulley, with one end going vertically downward from O to connect to A, and the other end going obliquely downward from O to connect to B; in the figure rope OA is in the vertical direction, rope OB is steeper relative to the straight rod, and the problem statement gives that the angle between rope OB and the straight rod is 30°. Reasoning: Let the tension in the rope be T, and the masses of rings A and B be m_A and m_B respectively. Analyze the forces on ring A alone: it is subject to gravity m_A g vertically downward, the tension T of rope OA vertically upward, and the support force of the straight rod on the ring perpendicular to the straight rod. Projecting along the direction of the straight rod, since the straight rod makes 30° with the horizontal and the angle between the vertical direction and the straight rod is 60°, the equilibrium condition is T cos60° = m_A g cos60°, giving T = m_A g. Analyze the forces on ring B alone: it is subject to gravity m_B g vertically downward, the tension T of rope OB along the BO direction, and the support force of the straight rod perpendicular to the straight rod. Projecting along the direction of the straight rod, the angle between rope OB and the straight rod is 30°, so the component of the tension upward along the straight rod is T cos30°; the component of gravity downward along the straight rod is m_B g sin30°. The equilibrium condition is T cos30° = m_B g sin30°, that is, T·√3/2 = m_B g·1/2, so T = m_B g/√3. The same light rope passes over a smooth fixed pulley, so the tension is the same; therefore m_A g = m_B g/√3, giving m_A:m_B = 1:√3.
